subject: SLO & Benchmark Protocol for FinLytics POC
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 15 Jan 2025 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: SLO & Benchmark Protocol for FinLytics POC

Hi Sarah — great to meet you and the team today. Quick recap from our discovery: FinLytics is prioritizing low-variance tail latency for real-time scoring in trading signals and wants to validate throughput for a concurrent inference profile. You mentioned target SLOs of p95 <= 120ms for 512-token streaming responses, and sustained throughput of ~400 concurrent requests (average sequence length ~350 tokens) during market hours.

To make the POC results reproducible on our side, could you confirm the following and share the benchmark materials you referenced on the call?
- Canonical prompt sets (typical, adversarial, and long-tail) — format (JSONL?), number of examples per bucket.
- Definition of "streaming" for your use case (chunk size, preferred tokenization boundary).
- Any pre/post-processing steps we should replicate (token filtering, reranker rules).
- Baseline environment you want us to match (network egress constraints, region, client concurrency shaping).

If you can drop the prompt sets and the baseline CSV, Marcus and I will prepare a measurement plan: workload generator config, KV cache warmup, steady-state warmup period, and exact latency percentiles we'll publish. Proposed next steps: you share artifacts by Friday 1/17, Marcus runs an initial baseline, then we sync for validation on Tuesday 1/21.

Thanks — I’ll also loop in Monica from CS for integration touchpoints.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[d] +1 415-555-0123

From: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@finlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Cc: Michael Gupta <michael.gupta@finlytics.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jan 2025 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLO & Benchmark Protocol for FinLytics POC

Dylan — thanks for the notes and the quick turnaround. Confirming targets from our side: p50 ~18ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms for streaming responses with incremental token emission. Concurrency: target 400 sustained with 4k/sec token ingress (approx).

Attached is the high-level requirements PDF and a CSV excerpt of your current baseline (we ran a smoke test last month). The prompt bundles are in JSONL with three buckets: "normal" (1k examples), "edge" (300 examples), and "long" (200 examples). Each JSONL line is: {"id":..., "prompt":..., "expected_behavior":...}.

Two clarifications:
- Streaming: we expect chunked responses at ~32 token boundaries with latency measured from request arrival to first-byte (TTFB) and to last-byte.
- Warmup: our infrastructure has a cold-start window — please include a 5-minute warmup and then run 20 minutes steady-state for each test slice.

Attaching: finlytics_benchmark_requirements.pdf; baseline_results.csv.

—Sarah Tan
Head of ML Engineering, FinLytics
[s] sarah.tan@finlytics.com
[Attachment: finlytics_benchmark_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: baseline_results.csv (text/csv)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@finlytics.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 17 Jan 2025 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO & Benchmark Protocol for FinLytics POC

Thanks for the files, Sarah — very helpful. A couple of technical items I want to lock down before we run anything so results are apples-to-apples: 

1) Measurement definitions: we will report TTFB, time-to-last-byte, and per-token inter-arrival percentiles. For streaming p95, do you want us to report p95(TTFB) and p95(per-token-latency) separately, or a combined metric? We recommend both.

2) Tokenization: please confirm tokenizer (BPE / model-specific) and whether we should apply any post-token filtering. If the prompt JSONL contains raw text, we will tokenize using the model's canonical tokenizer and attach token counts to each result row.

3) Concurrency shaping: to emulate production, we plan to use Poisson arrival with a mean matching your specified 400 concurrent steady-state. If you prefer a constant concurrency model (fixed worker count), say so — that changes batching and KV-cache behavior.

4) Load generator: we have two harnesses: an internal harness (reproducible config file, deterministic seeds) and a wrapped k6/Locust profile for distributed runs. Would you prefer the internal harness artifacts checked into your Drive link for reproducibility?

Proposed publication format: CSV with columns [test_id, bucket, tokenizer_tokens, ttfb_ms, lastbyte_ms, per_token_ms_p50,p95,p99, throughput_rps, run_config_link]. We will include raw histograms and latency heatmaps in the Drive folder.

If all good, we’ll start baseline runs Monday 1/20 and share initial plots on Tuesday 1/21.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_measurement_schema.txt (text/plain)]
From: Michael Gupta <michael.gupta@finlytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@finlytics.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jan 2025 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLO & Benchmark Protocol for FinLytics POC

Marcus — thanks. A few quick answers from eng: we want both metrics (TTFB and per-token p95). Tokenizer is the standard GPT-style BPE; prompts are raw text so tokenization on your side is fine. For concurrency shaping, we prefer Poisson arrivals to mimic burstiness.

Also: streaming chunk size should target 32 tokens but please document actual chunk sizes and observed framing latency. We attached a small baseline CSV (baseline_results.csv) with our internal tests — use it as the initial compare-to.

One more ask: can you include a reproducible seed and/or run id for each run so we can cross-check sample IDs? If you commit harness configs to the Drive link, please tag them with run ids.

—Michael
Michael Gupta
Senior Eng Lead, FinLytics
[Attachment: baseline_results.csv (text/csv)]
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: SLO & Benchmark Protocol for FinLytics POC

Team — thanks for the confirmations and the artifacts. Quick operational plan & next steps: 

1) Marcus will run the internal harness on Monday 1/20 (Poisson arrivals, 5-minute warmup, 20-minute steady-state per bucket) and produce the CSV with the schema he outlined. We will include run_id and reproducible seeds for each test.

2) Deliverables by EOD 1/21: initial plots (TTFB and per-token percentiles), raw CSVs, histogram artifacts, and a short write-up of environment parity (region, instance sizing, quantization, batching knobs).

3) Follow-up sync: Wed 1/22 10:00AM ET to validate results and pick the canary config if numbers look good. I’ll send a calendar invite shortly.

4) Procurement: we’ll copy procurement@finlytics.com on any DocuSign links for the POC order once you confirm budget band.

If anything changes on your side (e.g., different tokenizer or additional preproc), please flag asap. Otherwise we’ll proceed as planned.

Best —Dylan
